title: Hippocrates of Kos
summary: Hippocrates was a Greek physician from the island of Kos. The U.S. National Library of Medicine says his name and image emerged in the 5th century BCE, and that the Hippocratic Corpus, the collected writings attributed to him, contains about sixty works on medical topics.

uncertainty.note: Birth and death dates are traditional. The Dictionary of Scientific Biography gives 460 and c. 370 BCE; Britannica gives c. 460 and c. 375 BCE; the NLM page gives only the 5th century BCE. A 10-year band is used. Astronomical years: 460 BCE = -459, 370 BCE = -369.

as_recorded.value: (b Cos, 460 b.c.; d. Larissa, ca. 370 b.c.)

where.historical_name: Kos (Insel), island of the Asclepiads' medical school; no polity name is given by the sources opened

importance.justification: The National Library of Medicine states that Hippocrates is generally credited with turning away from divine notions of medicine toward observation, and that the Hippocratic Corpus contains about sixty works attributed to him, though probably by several authors.
